$schema_note: Canonical DomainSpec code ontology (L1) — the closed vocabulary of meta-types and typed relationships a feature concept-graph is built from. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH: TAXONOMY.md and RELATIONSHIPS.md are human-readable views of this file; validate_ontology.py enforces it. Reconciled from the DomainSpec paper (§4) and the framework repo (TAXONOMY.md / RELATIONSHIPS.md) on 2026-06-09. Where they disagreed, the repo (what ships and is enforced) won; see provenance.

provenance.paper: domainspec-paper.md §4 — 24 meta-types (13 backend + 11 UI), 26 edges (12 R_B + 8 R_U + 6 R_X). The paper gave NO signatures for the 8 intra-UI edges and had NO cross-feature family.
provenance.repo: TAXONOMY.md (25 meta-types) + RELATIONSHIPS.md (29 edges). Strict superset of the paper: adds the Saga meta-type and the three cross-feature edges, and supplies the 8 intra-UI signatures the paper lacked.
provenance.reconciliation: Adopt the repo superset as canonical (25 meta-types, 29 edges). Split the repo's '15 backend edges' into 12 true-backend + 3 cross-feature, making the edge-family partition honest (the paper's R = R_B + R_U + R_X could not express backend@A->backend@B edges). canonical_token uses the paper's CamelCase identifiers; display_name uses the repo's spaced/slashed form — this IS the token map the audit flagged as missing.
provenance.known_divergence: As of 2026-06-09 the framework repo's l1-extractor agent and audit_richness.py were reconciled to 25/29 (the agent count line fixed; audit_richness gained the 3 cross-feature signatures and dropped the phantom Aggregate/Governance types). Remaining gaps are follow-ups, not count divergences: (a) no CI gate runs a signature validator over docs/features/*/_categorical/L1.json; (b) this bundle's validator reads a generic {nodes, edges, type} graph, whereas the extractor emits {objects, morphisms, rel_type} L1.json — an adapter is needed to type-check real extractions; (c) RELATIONSHIPS.md still presents 3 edge groups (15 backend) while this JSON splits the 4th family (R_CF) out. This bundle is self-contained and authoritative for a scaffolded project.

partitions.backend: Server-side domain concepts (the L1 domain model).
partitions.ui: Client-side concepts. Disjoint from backend (Property P2).

meta_types.definition: Identity-bearing domain object with a lifecycle.
Identity-less reusable concept (Money, Address).
Finite set of states or categories.
Business action that changes state (a mutation).
Reads data without side effects.
Derives a value from inputs.
Business constraint or validation that gates actions.
Decision logic that selects behavior.
Multi-step orchestration of operations within a feature.
Cross-feature transactional orchestration. (Repo extension; not in the paper.)
API boundary — REST, GraphQL, or module contract.
Notification that something happened in the domain.
Data transformation between shapes across a boundary.
States + transitions + guards + effects governing an entity lifecycle.
Routable URL view with layout and auth gate.
Reusable page shell (sidebar, header, slot).
Composable UI building block with typed props.
Shaped data optimized for rendering.
Encapsulated reactive data/state logic.
Schema-validated user input contract.
User-triggered mutation or navigation.
Client-side access gate (auth, permissions).
Named connection between a hook and an API endpoint.
Data-shape transformation at the UI boundary.
Visual encoding of domain state (badge, icon, color).

edge_families.R_B: Backend — both endpoints are backend meta-types, within one feature.
edge_families.R_CF: Cross-feature — both endpoints are backend meta-types, across a feature/bounded-context boundary (source@A -> target@B). Not present in the paper; the honest 4th family.
edge_families.R_U: Intra-UI — both endpoints are UI meta-types.
edge_families.R_X: Cross-layer — source is a UI meta-type, target is a backend meta-type. Unidirectional UI -> backend (Property P3).

edges.semantics: An entity initiates / is the actor of an operation.
An operation emits an event upon completion.
A rule constrains when an operation can execute.
A calculation derives values used by an operation.
An event triggers a state transition.
An interface makes an operation or query accessible.
A workflow coordinates multiple operations.
A policy governs how an operation behaves.
A mapping transforms data between shapes.
An entity embeds a value object as a field.
A query reads data from an entity.
An entity is the source of a domain event.
An operation in feature A mutates/projects data into an entity owned by feature B.
An event in feature A triggers an operation owned by feature B.
A rule in feature A constrains whether feature B can execute an operation.
A page renders components as interactive islands.
A layout wraps pages, providing the visual shell.
A component includes child components.
A component consumes a hook for data/state.
A form validates input then delegates to an action.
An adapter transforms API data into a view model.
A guard controls access to a page.
A component renders data from a view model.
A binding fetches data from a backend query.
A binding invokes a backend operation.
A UI indicator mirrors a domain lifecycle state.
A view model is derived from entity fields.
A form schema aligns with an interface endpoint.
A client-side guard mirrors a backend access rule.

properties.name: Type safety
properties.statement: Every edge instance (a, r, b) respects r's signature: type(a) in source-set, type(b) in target-set.

properties.name: Partition disjointness
properties.statement: Backend and UI meta-types are disjoint; every meta-type belongs to exactly one partition.

properties.name: Cross-layer unidirectionality
properties.statement: Every R_X edge has a UI source and a backend target. UI depends on backend, never the reverse.

properties.name: Cross-feature is backend-to-backend
properties.statement: Every R_CF edge has a backend source and a backend target, crossing a feature boundary (source@A -> target@B).

properties.name: Edge-family partition
properties.statement: The edge set is the disjoint union R = R_B + R_CF + R_U + R_X; every edge belongs to exactly one family.
